description: >-
  FOXRED1 (FAD-dependent oxidoreductase domain-containing protein 1) is a nuclear-encoded
  flavoprotein of the mitochondrial inner membrane that functions as a complex I-specific
  assembly factor (molecular chaperone) required for biogenesis of the respiratory chain
  NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase (complex I). It belongs to the FAD-dependent oxidoreductase
  (DAO/FAD-NAD(P)-binding) structural family, carries an FAD cofactor, and is annotated as an
  oxidoreductase (EC 1.-.-.-), but no in-vivo catalytic substrate or reaction has been defined
  and it is not a structural subunit of the mature 44-subunit holoenzyme. FOXRED1 acts at the
  mid-late stages of complex I assembly, transiently associating with assembly intermediates
  and complex I subunits; in its absence, a late (~815 kDa) intermediate fails to mature and
  instead degrades to a smaller (~475 kDa) subcomplex, and cells accumulate only residual
  complex I. Biallelic loss-of-function variants cause mitochondrial complex I deficiency,
  nuclear type 19 (MC1DN19), an autosomal-recessive infantile-onset encephalomyopathy.

core_functions:
- description: >-
    Complex I-specific assembly factor with an FAD-dependent oxidoreductase fold. FOXRED1 is
    required for the mid-late stage of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I
    (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) biogenesis, transiently associating with complex I
    subunits; without it a late (~815 kDa) intermediate fails to mature to the holoenzyme and
    breaks down to a ~475 kDa subcomplex, leaving only residual complex I. It is not a subunit
    of the mature enzyme, so NADH dehydrogenase activity is deliberately NOT assigned. Its
    molecular activity is captured only at the generic oxidoreductase level
    (DAO/FAD-NAD(P)-binding family, EC 1.-.-.-): no substrate or reaction is known, and the original
    description of FOXRED1 as a "molecular chaperone" rests on its assembly requirement, not on
    a demonstrated protein-folding activity, so protein folding chaperone (GO:0044183) is not
    assigned.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0016491
    label: oxidoreductase activity
  directly_involved_in:

  - reference_id: PMID:25678554

  - reference_id: PMID:20858599
    supporting_text: >-

  knowledge_gaps:
  - gap_statement: >-
      The physiological substrate, catalytic reaction, and EC sub-subclass of FOXRED1's
      oxidoreductase activity are undetermined, as is whether its redox activity (rather than
      a purely structural/chaperone role of the fold) is required for complex I assembly.
    boundary: >-
      It is firmly established that FOXRED1 has an FAD-dependent oxidoreductase fold, carries
      FAD, and is required for complex I assembly; what is unknown is the reaction it catalyzes.
    gap_kind:
    - BIOLOGY
    dark_aspect: MF_DARK
    provenance:
    - reference_id: file:human/FOXRED1/FOXRED1-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: "EC=1.-.-.-;"
- description: >-
    FAD (flavin adenine dinucleotide) binding. FOXRED1 is a flavoprotein whose FAD/NAD(P)-binding
    fold binds an FAD cofactor (by similarity), consistent with its Flavoprotein/FAD keywords.
    This molecular function is not currently in GOA; it is added here on the basis of the UniProt
    COFACTOR annotation and the DAO/FAD-binding domain architecture.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0050660
    label: flavin adenine dinucleotide binding

  supported_by:

    record_section: ["CC:COFACTOR"]
    supporting_text: "Name=FAD; Xref=ChEBI:CHEBI:57692; Evidence={ECO:0000250};"
proposed_new_terms: []
suggested_questions:
- question: >-
    What is FOXRED1's actual enzymatic reaction and physiological substrate, and does its
    FAD-dependent redox chemistry contribute to complex I assembly, or does the fold act as a
    non-catalytic FAD-stabilized scaffold/chaperone?
- question: >-
    At the mid-late (~815 kDa to mature) transition, which specific complex I subunit(s) or
    assembly intermediate does FOXRED1 act on, and how do the MC1DN19 hypomorphic variants
    (R352W, N430S) perturb this step?
suggested_experiments:
- description: >-
    In vitro reconstitution with purified recombinant FOXRED1 and FAD, screening candidate
    substrates (e.g. complex I subunits or intermediates) by mass spectrometry / redox assays
    to define the catalyzed reaction and EC subclass, and testing whether catalytically dead
    (FAD-binding-pocket) mutants still support complex I assembly in FOXRED1-null cells.
- description: >-
    Complexome profiling / cross-linking MS in FOXRED1-null versus rescued cells to map which
    assembly intermediate accumulates or is destabilized and to identify FOXRED1's direct
    binding partner within the mid-late complex I assembly pathway.

evidence_object.statement: The original human fibroblast study linked FOXRED1 loss to complex I deficiency and rescued the defect by re-expression; its complex-I-specific framing describes that study, while later myoblast experiments found a contextual complex II effect.
evidence_object.supporting_text: Silencing of FOXRED1 in human fibroblasts resulted in reduced complex I

evidence_object.statement: FOXRED1 is required for the mid-late stages of complex I assembly; FOXRED1-null cells retain only ~10% complex I and cannot grow on galactose, a late ~815 kDa intermediate fails to mature and degrades to ~475 kDa, and FOXRED1 co-immunoprecipitates with complex I subunits.
